model_description: Autoregressive scratchpad decoder (~11M params, d_model 384, 8 layers, 8 heads) with Abacus digit-position embeddings, widened to 20-digit operands for tier 5. Computes a*b mod p by base-10 interleaved multiply-reduce (Horner over the digits of b, twenty steps): acc=0; for each digit b_i MSB->LSB, m_i=a*b_i, t_i=acc*10+m_i, acc=t_i mod p; R=acc. Never forms the full product; every step is the trivial a*single-digit multiply, which is what makes it learnable and length-scalable. Identical algorithm to recurrent_v4 with one literal changed (WIDTH 10->20), so it scales to ~20-digit operands (p < 2^64 < 10^20). Same algorithm for every prime and every operand length -> generalizes to unseen primes. For p>=1e20 emits 0.
training_description: WIDTH-20 base-10 interleaved-Horner scratchpad (recurrent_v5) -- the tier-4 recipe widened to twenty-digit operands, warm-started from the recurrent_v4 checkpoint (the per-step operation is identical, only the sequence length grows). Trained with a held-out split (disjoint train/val prime pools per tier) so reported accuracy is generalization to UNSEEN primes, with an operand-length curriculum 1->20 digits and tier-5-weighted sampling, then a finishing LR anneal. Because tiers 3-5 draw from thousands-to-quintillions of primes, the official benchmark primes are effectively unseen to this model, so generalization is what scores. The model generates the Horner chain-of-thought and returns the final acc. Teacher-forced next-token, loss on completion only. a%p,b%p legal two-operand reductions; answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation); no hand-coded arithmetic, no Barrett/Montgomery/CRT, no lookups. See dev/train_recurrent.py.
